newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOCKEY-AUSTRALIANS TAKE CHARGE IN CHAMPIONS' TROPHY.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-AUSTRALIANS TAKE CHARGE IN CHAMPIONS' TROPHY.

text.p: Shooting of the highest quality by Alyson Annan and Jennifer Morris saw Olympic champions Australia back to their winning ways with a 2-0 success over the Netherlands on the second day of the women's Champions' Trophy on Monday.

Annan started and finished a brilliant Australian attack just as the first half seemed set to be goalless. Morris hit a rasping corner shot in the 50th minute which was deflected high into the Dutch goal by the runner-out.
It was a a hard physical game with each side claiming three corners. Four players, three of them Dutch, were given temporary suspensions.

Australia's fifth win in their last six matches against the Dutch took them to the top of the rankings with four points from two games. They head the United States on goal difference. The Americans are proving the surprise packet. They followed their win over South Korea, with a 2-2 draw against Germany.

The U.S. showed the value of superb conditioning, coming back from 2-0 goals down to get their point. They had good fortune for their equalising goal in the 60th minute. Germany were penalised for taking too long over a free and the Americans took advantage for Kelly James to lob the ball past the German goalkeeper.
Germany had gone ahead with a subtle deflection in the 17th minute by Inga Moller and a solo effort by Natascha Keller four minutes into the second half.

Tara Maguire scored the Americans' first goal 12 minutes into the second half. Germany's second successive draw left them in fifth place ahead only of Britain who lost for the second day running, going down 2-0 to South Korea, the Olympic silver medallists.
Britain played well until they ran out of steam in the last quarter of the game. The Korea snapped up their goals in the last 10 minutes through Eun-kyung Choi and Jo-young Lee.
Tuesday a rest day with the tournament resuming on Wednesday when Australia play Britain.
